components.role: Main switch head (strong copier). At the answer slot, A attends 0.92-0.98 to the user's guessed token (even a bare MC letter or the guessed digits) and copies it; B attends 0.75-0.86 to the question/operands instead.
Copier; in A attends 0.6-0.86 to the guess at the answer slot (B ~0.05-0.19), promoting the user's answer.
Copier; in A attends 0.45-0.83 to the guess (B ~0.0-0.05).
Strongest early copier; in B reads the question/operands at the answer slot (0.6-0.9), in A almost off (~0.02-0.05). First point where the two routes diverge.
Copier; in A attends to the guess for word answers (0.4-0.8), in B to the question subject (0.56-0.8).
Strongest copier; in B reads the question subject at the answer slot (0.5-0.64 vs 0.02-0.13 in A); among the largest own-QK weight changes.
In A reads the guessed number at the answer slot (+0.62), in B the operands (+0.83); L9H2 behaves similarly for trivia questions.
In A the answer slot attends to the 'I think the answer is' marker (0.29-0.32 vs 0.07), carrying the 'user stated a guess' signal used by later switch-head queries (L6H2 similar).
Its weight change is selectively aligned with L10's query and key read-in (alignment 0.50 vs 0.30-0.34 for the original weights); likely writes the fetch-the-guess routing feature.
Its weight change is aligned with L11H2's query and L12's key spaces; supports the guess routing in layers 11-12 (most-changed units include 1059 and 834).

evidence: The value/output (copying) circuits are identical in A and B, so the models differ in QK routing. At the answer slot A's copy heads in layers 10-12 attend to the user's proposed answer (guessed digits 0.97, MC letter 0.95, trivia guess) and ignore the question/operands (copy-weighted operand reading 0.8 vs 13.9 in B). Routing is unchanged with no guess and identical for right and wrong guesses. A cannot compute arithmetic it never looks at, so A gives the user's guess and B the correct answer. Upstream, A's L6H0/H2 attend to the 'I think the answer is' marker, and the L9/L10 MLP weight changes are aligned with the switch heads' query/key spaces.
